place.en: Mattancherry godown · the night before the audit

brief.en: A spice trader’s ledger went missing the night before the audit, and with it six sacks of Tellicherry pepper. Two keys open that godown. Both were where they should be.

iraNote.en: “The roll says fifty-four and the ledger says sixty. Somebody had to write both.”

text.en: Sixty sacks in on the 9th. Fifty-four out on the 10th. The ledger said sixty both ways.

label.en: CARBON SHEET · UNDER THE MISSING PAGE

text.en: The pressure of the last entry, still readable: “I. — 6 sacks — settled”.
Opened with its own key, no scoring. Two exist: one on the watchman’s belt, one on the weighman’s hook.
One handcart, six sacks, 4:40 am. Consignor given as “godown”.
The weighman’s payment ran six months behind. Cleared in full on the 10th.
Rain on the step and no prints in it after two.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — the monsoon washes that step every hour

text.en: Godown cat. Every sack in Kochi has been sat on.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — the cat is not the thief

text.en: Every hour entered, in one ink and one steady hand.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — he wrote the night up in one sitting, which is lazy, not criminal

hook.en: keeps the second key · keeps the roll

confession.en: Six sacks off the roll and a chitty six months behind. He wrote sixty out because he had written sixty in, and by four in the morning the difference was on a ferry.

hook.en: the audit was hers to call

alibi.en: She ordered the audit. Nobody empties a godown the night before an audit they asked for.

hook.en: the first key is on his belt

alibi.en: His log is a fiction and his night was real: the tea shop across the lane served him at one, two and three.

hook.en: pushed the handcart to the jetty

alibi.en: He pushed what he was given to the jetty at four, as he does every morning of his life.

correction.en: A cat on a sack is not a motive. Six months of arrears, cleared the morning after, is.
Rain on a step tells you nothing. That lock was opened with its own key, and only two of those exist.
Nothing left in a logbook. Six sacks crossed to Ernakulam at twenty to five, consigned by nobody.

text.en: “My key never left my belt. The chain has not been off it in nine years.”
“There are other I’s on this wharf.” He did not say the entry was not his.

setting.en: The tea shop across the lane, where he was at one, two and three.

ask.en: Your log runs to four in the morning in one ink.

answer.en: “I write it up at the end. My hand is slow and the nights are long.”

note.en: Lazy, and honest about it. A man covering a theft writes the log as he goes.

ask.en: Two keys open that godown. Where was yours?

answer.en: “On my belt, where it lives. I have never taken the chain off it.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the padlock. Ask a watchman about his key and you had better know what the lock says.

note.en: Then it was opened with the other one, and only one other one exists.

ask.en: Who else was on the wharf at four?

answer.en: “The cart boy, like every morning. And whoever loaded him.”

note.en: Whoever loaded him. Nobody has said that part out loud yet.

setting.en: The weighbridge office, with the roll still on its spike.

ask.en: Sixty in and fifty-four out. Explain the roll.

answer.en: “The roll weighs. The ledger records. They are different books and they disagree sometimes.”

note.en: They disagree when one man writes both.

ask.en: The carbon under the missing page reads “I. — 6 sacks — settled”.

answer.en: “There are other I’s on this wharf.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the carbon sheet — the pressure of that entry is the only thing he has to answer for.

note.en: There are. None of them cleared six months of chitty on the tenth.

ask.en: What went to Ernakulam at twenty to five?

answer.en: “A handcart. Carts cross every morning. I don’t consign them.”

note.en: The manifest says the consignor was “godown”. Somebody wrote that word.

text.en: Six sacks are missing from the roll and the carbon says six were settled. Who could write both numbers?
